summary.text: This briefing evaluates combining gaussian process, kolmogorov arnold networks, and regression for uncertainty-aware scientific machine learning. By integrating sparse variational Gaussian process inference into the Kolmogorov-Arnold network topology, the combined model enables scalable Bayesian inference and propagates uncertainty through deep additive structures using analytic moment matching. The DVF axis scores are D: 3.0, F: 3.0, and V: 3.0.

target_user.text: The target users are engineers, researchers, and technical developers working on scientific machine learning, automated process modeling, and computer vision tracking, as evidenced by patent assignees and repository toolsets.

jtbd.text: Perform uncertainty-aware regression and scientific function approximation in deep architectures while distinguishing aleatoric from epistemic uncertainty.

value_prop.text: Standard implementations of Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks lack principled uncertainty quantification capabilities that are essential for scientific applications. The integrated architecture provides scalable Bayesian inference with computational complexity quasi-linear in sample size while preserving interpretability.

riskiest_assumption.text: The riskiest assumption, driven by feasibility score F: 3.0, is that analytic moment matching and sparse variational Gaussian process inference can scale effectively across complex Kolmogorov-Arnold network topologies without severe degradation in approximation accuracy or convergence stability.

mvp.text: Build a technical proof of concept script combining sparse variational Gaussian processes with a Kolmogorov-Arnold network layer using existing packages to test regression performance and epistemic uncertainty calibration on a standard benchmark.
mvp.type: technical proof of concept from existing packages

success_metric.text: Achieve a proposed threshold of negative log-likelihood reduction by at least 15 percent compared to standard MLPs while maintaining a correlation of calibration error below a proposed threshold of 0.05 on held-out test data.

kill_criteria.text: If training time scales worse than O(NM^2) with respect to sample size N and inducing points M, violating the quasi-linear complexity expectation, the approach is killed.

If epistemic uncertainty estimates fail to distinguish out-of-distribution inputs from in-distribution data, achieving an area under the ROC curve below a proposed threshold of 0.60, the approach is killed.

open_source.use: Provides core machine learning utilities and foundational regression building blocks to support model training loops.
Used to compute and evaluate calibration metrics for the probabilistic outputs generated by the combined network.

to_build.text: Develop a custom analytic moment matching layer that bridges sparse variational Gaussian process distributions with the learnable univariate functions on Kolmogorov-Arnold network edges.
